title: Taking my agents off the tracker API with a queue in git
summary: Plane rate-limited every agent session at once because they shared one key. Now agents write a file to a queue, and one job applies the writes at a pace the API accepts.

stat.label: intents applied from the queue, read on 2026-11-18, with none failed or pending

sections.heading: Problem
paragraphs: Plane allows 120 calls a minute per key, and every agent session shared one key. On 7 November a burst of sessions used the allowance and every one of them was limited.

sections.heading: What I built
paragraphs: Threads no longer call Plane. To change an item, a thread commits one JSON file to a queue directory. Each file is one intent, so two threads never conflict. The operations are a closed list: close, state, comment, update, create and cycle.

A drain job runs on a runner in my network every ten minutes and on any push that touches the queue, and never on a pull request. It applies the oldest intent first, at most 60 calls a minute and 60 intents a run. The key comes from Vault at run time. State moves forward only. A hidden marker on each comment makes a replay safe.
To read, a thread opens a mirror file in the same repository. The mirror records when it was taken and keeps the last good detail file when a read fails.

sections.heading: Result
paragraphs: On 18 November the queue held 330 applied intents: 106 comments, 62 closes, 59 updates, 59 creates, 41 state changes and 3 cycle changes. It held none failed and none pending. A failed intent lands in a failed directory and makes the run exit non-zero, so a bad write cannot pass as a green run.

sections.heading: Lesson
paragraphs: A shared credential needs one place that spends it. Put the writes in git, where they are reviewable, and let one slow worker talk to the API.
